title: Artifact Display, Annotation, and Distance Measurement
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement 3 procedural “artifacts”: a vase (a solid of revolution using LatheGeometry), a plate (disc + edge rim), and a small figurine (a composite mesh assembled from multiple spheres).

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Display and Annotations]
(1) Artifact selector id="artifactSelect": the options correspond to the three artifacts (e.g., vase, plate, figurine).
(2) Turntable: the selected object rotates around the vertical axis; automatic rotation switch id="autoRotate" (checkbox or toggle).
(3) Place 5 clickable hotspots (small red dots/Sprites) on each artifact. When clicked, display descriptive text in a popup or fixed panel.
(4) Distance measurement tool: the user clicks two points on the surface in sequence, records the measurement result in __3D_STATE__.measurements (e.g., [{a,b,distance},...]), and displays it briefly in the UI.

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - currentArtifact: string
  - annotationCount: number (the number of hotspots on the current artifact; should be 5)
  - selectedAnnotation: number | null (0–4 or null)
  - autoRotate: boolean
  - measurements: Array (measurement records; the structure may be defined as needed but must include a numeric distance)
  - artifactSize: { w: number, h: number, d: number } (estimated bounding dimensions of the current artifact)

Output a single HTML file.
